issues.legal_issue: Buildings situated on land used in common by their occupants form one common compound for measuring proximity to a public water supply, without requiring that the shared land be appurtenant to each building.
material_facts: The company’s factory, residential buildings, and other facilities stood within a common area used by the occupants for access and other shared purposes.
The occupants’ common use of the area was not disputed.
Part of the common area was within the prescribed distance of a public stand pipe.
issues.conclusion: The buildings in the common compound were to be treated together for the distance test; because part of the common compound was within the prescribed distance, the whole complex fell within the water-tax levy.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 128(1)(x) and 129(a) of the Uttar Pradesh Municipalities Act, 1916 authorize water-tax subject to the distance restriction in Section 129(a). Explanation (a) to Section 129 treats several buildings in a common compound together for that test. The first part of the Explanation, which includes a building’s own compound, is distinct from its second part, which covers a common compound; the latter does not require appurtenance under Sections 2(2) and 2(5). The Court noted the taxpayer-favouring construction principle associated with The Central India Spinning and Weaving and Manufacturing Co. Ltd. v. The Municipal Committee, Wardha; Commissioner of Income-Tax, Punjab v. Kulu Valley Transport Co. (P) Ltd.; Collector of Estate Duty v. M/s. R. Kanakasabai; and Polestar Electronic (P) Ltd. v. Addl. Commissioner, Sales Tax, Delhi, but held that the statutory language admitted only one interpretation.

rule.if: municipal_water_tax_assessment and multiple_buildings_on_shared_land and occupants_share_use_of_land and part_of_shared_land_within_water_service_area

predicates.municipal_water_tax_assessment: A municipality sought to assess buildings or land to a water-related municipal charge.
predicates.multiple_buildings_on_shared_land: Several buildings were situated on the same surrounding land.
predicates.occupants_share_use_of_land: The occupants of the buildings had a common right to use the surrounding land.
predicates.part_of_shared_land_within_water_service: Some part of the land shared by the occupants was within the applicable distance of a public water-supply point.

issues.definition: When a municipal water-tax assessment concerns several buildings on land their occupants share, and some of that land lies within the water-service area, all the buildings fall within the taxable unit.

issues.legal_issue: A writ court may set aside an appellate authority’s decision when it rests on a patent error of law, even though the writ court is not acting as an appellate court on the merits.
material_facts: The District Magistrate treated the company’s buildings as separate for water-tax purposes by relying on the definition of an appurtenant compound.
The District Magistrate did not consider the part of the statutory definition addressing several buildings in a common compound.
The single judge intervened, although the single judge’s own reasoning about appurtenance was not correct.
issues.conclusion: The single judge was justified in intervening because the District Magistrate’s omission produced a patent error of law; the single judge reached the correct result despite using an inaccurate line of reasoning.
issues.legal_principle: Under Articles 226 and 227 of the Constitution, the High Court does not act as a court of appeal, but may correct patent errors of law. The Court accepted that principle as supported by Shri Ambica Mills Co. Ltd. v. Shri S.B. Bhatt, Syed Yakoob v. K.S. Radhakrishnan, Bhutnath Chatterjee v. State of West Bengal, Mohd. Yunus v. Mohd. Mustaqim, and Harbans Lal v. Jagmohan Saran.

predicates.writ_review_of_appellate_tax_decision: A party sought writ review of an appellate authority’s decision concerning a tax assessment.
predicates.appellate_authority_omitted_relevant_sta: The appellate authority failed to consider a relevant part of the governing statutory definition.
predicates.omission_caused_patent_error_of_law: The failure to consider that definition materially affected the authority’s legal reasoning.

issues.definition: Writ interference is justified where an appellate tax decision omits a relevant statutory definition and that omission causes a patent error of law.

issues.legal_issue: Non-residential buildings may be subject to a municipal water-tax when the applicable local rules authorize the charge for all property types within the prescribed water-service area.
material_facts: The company challenged the inclusion of its factory premises on the ground that the relevant notification applied only to residential buildings; that contention had not been raised before the lower authorities.
The Court considered the issue because it went to the municipality’s authority to tax non-residential premises.

An additional affidavit and a printed booklet containing the local rules showed that the rules authorized water-tax for land and buildings within the prescribed distance, without limiting the charge to residential property.
The Court found no contrary notification and applied the presumption concerning the regular performance of official acts under Section 114 of the Indian Evidence Act.
issues.conclusion: The applicable notification and rules covered the factory premises as well as residential buildings, so the non-residential premises were within the water-tax levy.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 128(1)(x) and 129(a) of the Uttar Pradesh Municipalities Act, 1916, read with the local rules made under Section 296, permitted water-tax on land and buildings of all types within the prescribed distance. Section 114 of the Indian Evidence Act supported the presumption that the relevant official acts had been regularly performed. The Court considered the late-raised contention because it went to the root of the municipality’s authority to tax the premises.

predicates.municipal_water_tax_assessment: A municipality sought to assess property to a water-related municipal charge.
predicates.local_rules_cover_all_property_types: The applicable local rules authorized the charge for residential and non-residential property alike.
predicates.nonresidential_property_within_water_ser: The non-residential property was within the applicable distance of a public water-supply point.
predicates.authority_to_tax_nonresidential_property: A party challenged the municipality’s authority to charge the non-residential property.

issues.definition: Non-residential property is subject to the municipal water-tax when the local rules cover all property types, the property is within the water-service area, and the municipality’s authority to tax it is disputed.
